svg.font-family: Inter, Segoe UI, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif, Apple Color Emoji, Segoe UI Emoji, Noto Color Emoji
svg.title: The surface server
svg.desc: The surface server, started with chantier serve, is one process per planning surface and machine. The planning folder stays the only truth: plain JSON and Markdown, edited by the CLI, the agents, git and you, with no database; the server reads it and edits only the backlog and the configuration, through the CLI's own commands, never a batch. The process holds the web board with its published API (a WebSocket, and HTTP as the same protocol, behind a key: the private key reads and acts, the public key reads only), the forge hub, which reads the forge read-only at most every 20 s and appends journal lines, and the writer, which commits, rebases and pushes the surface's published paths within 5 minutes of a change. It reads the files cheaply: each project's state sits in memory behind a fingerprint of its folder, a walk of file stats with no file opened; the system's change notifications (watchfiles) say what moved; one walk follows once a project's files are quiet for 1 s, at most 5 s after the first change; the archives and the trash are read for their last folders only. Each session's watcher subscribes to the events of its project, reads only that project's journal lines and wakes its session. The clients are the web board, chantier live in a terminal and any API client.
svg.text: One process per planning surface and machine: it serves the plan, and the plan stays the only truth.
🌐 The web board and its published API

the archives and the trash: only their last folders; no notifications: a check every 5 s
reads the forge, read-only, with your own gh or glab, through the connector of its forge
at most every 20 s, and only while a client is subscribed
appends journal lines: a merge, a red CI, a wait met; runs no git, messages no agent
commits, rebases and pushes the surface's published paths (projects/, root chantier.yaml)
within 5 minutes of a change, with your own git identity and hooks, never forced
one writer per surface and machine, held by an OS lock

svg.text: The server never edits a batch and never messages an agent.
